title: Introduce energy-aware budget controller and autotune profiles for cost-efficient inference
author: Evan Brooks
release_notes: Adds an optional energy_budget parameter to the serving scheduler; new autotuner job that produces per-model cost/latency/energy profiles; console dashboard exposes watt-hour per-1000 tokens metric and recommended quant/profile; backward compatible by default.
body:
Motivation: Production customers increasingly ask for predictable unit economics under hard energy or cost constraints (edge deployments and corporate sustainability targets). This PR adds an energy-aware budget controller in the request routing/batching layer and a background 'autotune' that generates deployment profiles (batching, quantization, kernel preference) tailored for cost and energy minimization. The default behavior is opt-in; when enabled, the controller will nudge scheduling and model selection toward profiles that meet the provided energy_budget or cost_budget while respecting latency SLOs.

High level changes: 1) serving/energy_model.py - new energy estimation module that converts token throughput, kernel selection, and GPU power curves into estimated watt-hours per token. 2) serving/scheduler.py - energy_budget parameter and budget-aware backpressure/batching adjustments. 3) optimize/autotuner.py - periodic job that runs short synthetic workloads across supported GPUs to derive profiles ranked by unit cost and energy consumption. 4) model_registry/profiles.yaml - schema and a first set of sample profiles for llama-2-13b, redwood-mini, and gptx-7b-quant. 5) console: unit_econ_dashboard.md and an API extension to surface energy and recommended profile. 6) docs: quantization-profiles.md — guidance and safety notes about switching quantization profiles in production. 7) tests and CI workflows for the autotuner and scheduler.

Commits summary: - Add energy estimation primitives and GPU power curve loader - Wire energy-aware decisions into scheduler with feature flag - Implement autotuner job and profile serializer - Add e2e bench harness and lightweight unit econ metrics - Docs and console exposure for recommendations - Tests and CI: autotune workflow + hardware simulation tests

Files changed (high level): ["redwood/serving/energy_model.py", "redwood/serving/scheduler.py", "redwood/optimize/autotuner.py", "redwood/model_registry/profiles.yaml", "console/unit_econ_dashboard.md", "docs/quantization-profiles.md", "tests/unit/test_energy_budget.py", "tests/integration/test_autotuner_sim.py", "ci/workflows/autotune.yaml", "redwood/console/api/recommendations.py", "examples/autotune-runbook.md", "redwood/serving/flags.py"].

Benchmarks/Numbers: On a 16GB A10G-like profile in our perf-lab (synthetic chat workload, avg seq 128, concurrency 8) the autotuned profile + energy-aware batching reduced estimated GPU watt-hours/1k tokens by 10-14% and reduced token cost by 6-9% relative to baseline autoscheduler. Tail latency (p95) remained within 5% of baseline for latency-focused workloads when energy_budget was balanced; in strict energy_budget mode p95 increases were 12-18% for some models (documented in release notes and guarded behind the opt-in flag).

Testing: Unit tests cover energy math and the scheduler decision paths (test_energy_budget.py). Integration tests run the autotuner in simulation mode (no real GPUs) and validate profiles are produced and applied as expected. CI matrix includes a perf-canary job that ran with real perf-lab hardware; the initial canary failed due to a transient kernel mismatch on old drivers, we pinned the kernel selection in the autotuner and reran — CI now green.

Review thread (highlights): - Aisha: requested additional test coverage around mixed-precision fallbacks and explicit behavior when profiles are missing (commented in review). - Evan: added tests and a fallback that defaults to a conservative CPU-bound estimator when no GPU power curve present. - Marco: asked for clearer docs around safety (how to opt out, how to pin legacy profiles); doc changes added. - Dana: noted potential customer-facing naming implications ("energy_budget") and asked we surface both energy and currency units; UX change applied in console API.

Migration and rollout plan: Feature gated off by default. Flag is serving.use_energy_budget. Step 1: ship to Hosted as internal opt-in tenant (2 weeks). Step 2: enable perf-canary on Dedicated for a small customer subset and collect unit-econ deltas (4 weeks). Step 3: document tenant-level defaults and recommend runbooks for On-Prem. Autotuner runs as a low-priority batch job and stores profiles in model_registry/profiles.yaml; operators can pin a profile per-deployment.

Backward compatibility: All changes are opt-in. If energy_budget is not set, scheduler behavior is identical to current autoscheduler. Autotuner output is additive and does not overwrite existing pinned profiles without explicit operator action.

Action items for follow-ups (separate PRs): - Add support for multi-GPU profile aggregation (ENG-4702) - Add customer-facing billing mapping for energy metrics (PM-199) - Expose fine-grained kernel-power calibration tool in perf-lab.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the controller, autotuner, profile schema, docs, and tests. Kernel-level scheduling and driver-level power capping will be in a follow up.

References: Linear ENG-4621 (autotune design), internal perf runs in benchmark-lab, discussion in #infra-costs.
